emergency.notes: Mountain rescue / Alpine rescue: 1414 (REGA helicopter rescue). ADAC/TCS roadside assistance: 140. Emergency operators typically speak German, French, Italian, and English depending on the region.

travelAdvisory.summary: Exercise normal precautions in Switzerland. Switzerland is a stable, prosperous country with a high standard of safety for visitors.

travelAdvisoryUK.summary: Most visits to Switzerland are trouble-free. Take care in mountain areas and check avalanche forecasts in winter.

healthcare.costForTourists: Switzerland has world-class healthcare but it is extremely expensive. GP visit CHF 150-250. Emergency room CHF 500-2,000. Hospital stay CHF 1,000-4,000+/night. EU EHIC cards are not valid in Switzerland.
healthcare.pharmacyAccess: Pharmacies (Apotheke/Pharmacie) are ubiquitous. After-hours emergency pharmacies on rotating basis. Pharmacists typically speak German, French, or Italian plus English.
healthcare.hospitalNotes: Hospital quality is world-class. University hospitals in Zurich, Bern, Geneva, Basel, and Lausanne are internationally ranked. English is widely spoken in medical settings. Mountain rescue (REGA) provides helicopter emergency services.
vaccinationsRecommended: Tick-borne Encephalitis (TBE) if hiking in forested areas, spring-autumn
healthcare.insuranceAdvice: Travel insurance is essential. Switzerland has some of the most expensive healthcare costs in the world. Ensure your policy covers mountain rescue (REGA), as helicopter operations cost CHF 3,000-10,000+. Ski accident coverage is strongly recommended.

pharmacy.hours: Typically Mon-Fri 8am-6:30pm, Sat 8am-5pm. Some 24/7 pharmacies exist in major cities (e.g., in Zurich, Basel, Geneva). Look for 'Apotheke' or 'Pharmacie'.
pharmacy.tips: Pharmacists are well-trained and often speak English. Many common OTC medications are available without prescription. Bring a European Health Insurance Card (EHIC) if you're an EU citizen — it covers emergency care at public hospitals.

recommended: tick-borne encephalitis (if visiting rural areas in summer)
vaccinations.notes: No mandatory vaccinations for travelers. Ensure routine vaccinations are current. Tick encephalitis vaccination recommended if spending time outdoors in grassy or forested areas from April to October.

water.notes: Tap water is safe and high quality throughout Switzerland. Bottled water is widely available.

healthcare.foodSafetyTips: Switzerland has excellent food safety standards. Swiss chocolate, cheese, and meat are generally very safe. Be aware of high prices in restaurants — dining out is one of the world's most expensive.

travelInsurance.tips: Switzerland is extremely expensive. A hospital stay can cost 1,000-3,000 CHF per day. Travel insurance with medical evacuation coverage is essential — helicopter rescue (Rega) alone can cost 10,000+ CHF. EHIC covers EU citizens for emergency care at public facilities.

healthcare.qualityNotes: World-class healthcare with highly trained doctors. Switzerland has some of the best hospitals in Europe. English is widely spoken in medical settings. Healthcare is expensive — even routine visits can cost hundreds of CHF.

medications.prescriptionRules: Prescriptions from foreign doctors are generally accepted if from an EU/EEA country (translated). Prescriptions from outside Europe may need verification. Swiss prescriptions are valid at pharmacies.

restrictedMeds.name: Codeine-containing medications
restrictedMeds.note: Codeine is a controlled substance in Switzerland. Products with codeine require a prescription from a Swiss doctor. Small quantities for personal use may be allowed with proper documentation.

restrictedMeds.name: Tramadol
restrictedMeds.note: A controlled opioid. Requires a Swiss prescription for quantities beyond personal use allowance.

restrictedMeds.name: Benzodiazepines (e.g., Valium/diazepam)
restrictedMeds.note: Controlled substances. If you have a legitimate prescription from home, carry the original prescription and a doctor's letter. Swiss customs may require additional documentation.

restrictedMeds.name: Medical cannabis
restrictedMeds.note: Cannabis with THC is strictly controlled. Only available via Swiss prescription for specific medical conditions. CBD products with <1% THC are legal.

medications.bringDocumentation: Carry a doctor's letter in English (or German/French/Italian) listing all medications with generic names. Keep medications in original packaging. For controlled substances, carry the original prescription and a Schengen-style travel certificate if available.

scams.name: Fake alpine tour guides
scams.description: Unofficial 'guides' offer below-market prices for guided hikes or ski tours. These individuals are not certified and may lead tourists into dangerous situations.
scams.avoidance: Only use certified mountain guides (Bergführer) registered with the Swiss Mountain Guide Association. Check qualifications before booking.

scams.name: Expensive tourist menus
scams.description: Restaurants near tourist attractions offer 'tourist menus' at inflated prices. A cheese fondue can cost CHF 50-80 per person near the old town vs CHF 25-35 in local restaurants.
scams.avoidance: Walk one street away from main tourist areas. Check menus with prices posted outside before sitting. Ask locals for recommendations.

connectivity.simOptions: SIM cards from Sunrise, Salt, or Swisscom at airports and shops. EU roaming rules do not apply in Switzerland (not EU member). Tourist data SIM ~CHF 30-60 for 10-30GB. eSIM via Airalo.
connectivity.wifiAvailability: Free WiFi widely available in hotels, cafes, train stations, and many public areas. SBB trains have WiFi on major routes. SwissPass travelers get WiFi access on trains.
connectivity.bestOption: Salt prepaid SIM for best value. eSIM via Airalo. Remember Switzerland uses CHF (Swiss Franc), not Euros.

cultural.tipping: Service is included in Swiss prices by law. Tipping is not mandatory but leaving the small change (rounding up to nearest CHF 5) is polite. 5-10% is generous in restaurants.
cultural.dressCode: Smart casual is the norm. Swiss people dress neatly and conservatively. Cover up in churches. Fondue restaurants are casual.
cultural.greetings: Handshake in formal settings. Three cheek kisses (right-left-right) among friends, depending on the region. Use formal address (Sie/Sie or Monsieur/Madame) with strangers.
taboos: Making noise between 10pm and 7am — quiet hours are taken seriously
Not sorting recycling correctly — Switzerland has strict recycling laws
Swimming or sunbathing in inappropriate areas
Flushing the toilet after 10pm in apartment buildings (some cantons)
Rushing through a meal or eating on the go
cultural.haggling: Not practiced. Prices are fixed. Switzerland is known for high but fair pricing.

phrases.local: Ich verstehe nicht / Je ne comprends pas
Wie viel kostet das? / Combien ça coûte?
phrases.phonetic: vee feel kos-tet das / kom-byan sah koot

safety.lgbtSafety: Very LGBTQ+ friendly. Same-sex marriage legalized in 2022. Zurich and Geneva have vibrant LGBTQ+ communities. Zurich Pride is a major annual event.
safety.soloFemaleSafety: Very safe. Switzerland consistently ranks among the safest countries for women travelers. Normal precautions apply in cities at night.
safety.notes: Switzerland is one of the safest countries in the world. The main risk for tourists is natural disasters in the Alps (avalanches, falling rocks, sudden storms). Mountain activities require proper equipment, guides, and respect for weather forecasts.

practical.visaFreeCountries: US citizens: 90 days visa-free (Schengen). UK citizens: 90 days in 180-day period. EU citizens: unlimited as Schengen member.
practical.bestTimeToVisit: December-March for skiing. June-September for hiking and lake swimming. Spring (April-May) and autumn (September-October) for mild weather and fewer crowds.

hospitals.name: University Hospital Zurich (USZ)
hospitals.notes: One of Europe's leading university hospitals.

hospitals.name: Geneva University Hospitals (HUG)
hospitals.notes: French-speaking. Serves the international community in Geneva.

immediate: If caught, try to stay on the surface by swimming motions
As snow slows, cover your mouth and nose to create an air pocket
Spit to determine which way is up, then try to push a hand toward the surface
Stay calm to conserve oxygen — panic consumes air faster
If you see someone buried, mark the last-seen point and call 1414 immediately
after: Call REGA (1414) for helicopter rescue — they operate in all conditions
Follow Swiss Alpine Club (SAC) guidance for rescue operations
Do not attempt to go further into an avalanche-risk zone

immediate: Descend from mountain ridges and summits immediately — seek shelter in valleys
Avoid tall isolated trees, metallic objects, and open areas
If no shelter available, squat low on the balls of your feet with feet together — do not lie flat
Stay away from bodies of water during lightning
If in a vehicle, stay inside — it acts as a Faraday cage
after: Wait 30 minutes after the last thunder before resuming outdoor activity
Check MeteoSwiss app for forecast before resuming Alpine activities
